children.description: The API reference lists every public type, hook, factory method and modifier in Reactor. It is generated from the XML doc comments in the source code.
children.label: Overview

children.description: State, effects, context and the other hooks a component calls from Render.
children.label: Overview

children.description: Subscribes to an ObservableCollection and re-renders on Add/Remove/Reset. Returns the collection as IReadOnlyList.
children.label: UseCollection

children.description: Subscribes to an external store that exposes a current snapshot getter. Re-renders only when a change notification yields a different snapshot.
children.label: UseExternalStore

children.description: Subscribes to an INotifyPropertyChanged source and re-renders when any property changes. Returns the same source object.
children.label: UseObservable

children.description: Subscribes to a specific property on an INotifyPropertyChanged source. Re-renders only when that property changes.
children.label: UseObservableProperty

children.description: Observes an object and all nested INotifyPropertyChanged values reachable through its properties. Re-renders when any property at any depth changes. Automatically subscribes/unsubscribes as property values change.
children.label: UseObservableTree

children.description: Like UseState, but the value survives unmount/remount via an in-memory cache. On first mount, uses cached value if available, otherwise uses initialValue. Value is saved to cache on unmount.
children.label: UsePersisted

children.description: Returns a mutable ref object that persists across renders.
children.label: UseRef

children.description: Declares a piece of state. Returns (currentValue, setter). Must be called in the same order every render (just like React hooks).
children.label: UseState

children.description: Returns a stable callback reference that doesn't change between renders.
children.label: UseCallback

children.description: Runs a side effect after render. The effect re-runs when any dependency changes. Pass an empty array for "run once on mount" semantics. Returns a cleanup action that runs before the next effect or on unmount.
children.label: UseEffect

children.description: Memoizes a computed value, recomputing only when dependencies change.
children.label: UseMemo

children.description: Memoize cell construction keyed by keySelector. Cells are reused when both the item's key and value match the previous render. Keys that recur with mutated content rebuild that cell only. Reordered keys reuse cells (the reconciler's keyed- children path keeps the underlying control without unmount/remount).
children.label: UseMemoCellsByKey

children.description: Reads the nearest ancestor's provided value for the given context. Returns the context's DefaultValue if no provider exists in the ancestor chain. Follows hook rules — must be called in the same order every render.
children.label: UseContext

children.description: Returns an IntlAccessor for the current locale. Re-renders this component when the locale changes via a parent LocaleProvider. If no LocaleProvider is present, returns a default accessor using the OS locale. Uses Context internally — the context system handles re-renders automatically.
children.label: UseIntl

children.description: Creates a child validation context independent from any parent. Returns both the child context and the parent (if one exists). The child collects its own messages; use the parent reference to bubble manually.
children.label: UseChildValidationContext

children.description: Returns the nearest ancestor's ValidationContext, or creates a new one scoped to this component. The created context persists across re-renders.
children.label: UseValidationContext

children.description: Returns true when the given window's width is >= minWidth. Re-renders when the window resizes across the breakpoint.
children.label: UseBreakpoint

children.description: Returns the current display snapshot and re-renders when the display layout changes.
children.label: UseDisplays

children.description: Subscribes to the host window's activation events and re-renders on change. Returns true outside a window (the surface is "active" while shown). (spec 036 §7)
children.label: UseIsActive

children.description: Returns a covered hint from the host window's z-order transitions and re-renders on change. The value is not pixel-accurate occlusion state.
children.label: UseIsCovered

children.description: Applies a lifetime-bound width/height aspect lock to the owning window. Last mounted hook wins; unmounting restores the previous writer.
children.label: UseWindowAspectRatio

children.description: Returns a stable callback that starts a framework-managed window drag/move loop (cursor polling + AppWindow.Move at ~60Hz until the left mouse button is released).
children.label: UseWindowDragMove

children.description: Subscribes to the host window's PositionChanged event and re-renders on change. Returns (0, 0) outside a window. (spec 054 §5.5)
children.label: UseWindowPosition

children.description: Returns (width, height) of the given window and re-renders when the window resizes.
children.label: UseWindowSize

children.description: Returns true when the system is in a High Contrast (forced colors) theme. Automatically re-renders the component when high contrast is toggled.
children.label: UseHighContrast

children.description: Returns the high contrast scheme name (e.g., "High Contrast Black", "High Contrast White") or null if not in high contrast mode. Automatically re-renders the component when the scheme changes.
children.label: UseHighContrastScheme

children.description: Returns true when the user or system prefers reduced motion (e.g., Windows "Show animations" is off, or SPI_GETCLIENTAREAANIMATION returns false). Automatically re-renders the component when the preference changes.
children.label: UseReducedMotion

children.description: Creates and returns a FocusManager scoped to this component. The manager persists across re-renders.
children.label: UseFocus

children.description: Creates a focus trap handle that traps keyboard focus within a container when active. Use with the .FocusTrap() element modifier.
children.label: UseFocusTrap

children.description: Registers lifecycle callbacks that fire during navigation events.
children.label: UseNavigationLifecycle

children.description: Returns true when the current process is running with the in-app devtools UI enabled. This is the AND of two independent signals:
children.label: UseDevtools

children.description: The focus manager and the modifiers that the UseFocus hooks work with.
children.label: Focus helpers

children.description: Base class for stateful components (like React class components, but using hooks). Components hold a RenderContext that tracks their hook state across re-renders.
children.label: Component

children.description: A typed, named context that can be provided to a subtree and consumed by any descendant. Define as a static field. Provide via .Provide() modifier. Consume via UseContext() hook.
children.label: Context

children.description: Non-generic base for type-erased storage in the context scope stack.

children.description: Bridges WinUI's ItemsRepeater/IElementFactory to Reactor's Reconciler. GetElement calls the view builder then mounts; RecycleElement unmounts.

children.description: Represents either an explicit value or an unset state.
children.label: Optional

children.description: A mutable reference that persists across renders (like React's useRef).
children.label: Ref

children.description: Passed to function components and provides access to hooks. Each component instance gets its own RenderContext which tracks hook call order.
children.label: RenderContext

children.description: Application subclass that implements IXamlMetadataProvider so the native XAML schema context can resolve managed types from XBF theme resources. No App.xaml needed — XamlControlsResources are loaded programmatically. The IXamlMetadataProvider implementation delegates to the WinUI controls' built-in provider so that custom control types (TextCommandBarFlyout, etc.) can be instantiated from XBF theme resources.
children.label: ReactorApplication

children.description: Hosts a Reactor component tree inside a WinUI Window. Manages the render loop: when state changes, re-renders the component and reconciles the virtual tree against the real WinUI control tree.
children.label: ReactorHost

children.description: A fully self-contained WinUI ContentControl that hosts a Reactor component tree. Drop this into any vanilla WinUI app — no ReactorApp, ReactorApplication, or special bootstrapping needed. Each instance owns its own Reconciler and render loop.

children.description: Provides semantic theme tokens and custom resource references. All tokens resolve from WinUI's resource system and automatically adapt when the theme changes (Light ↔ Dark).
children.label: Theme

children.description: Lookup helpers for WinUI theme resources. These resolve against Application.Current.Resources, which includes all merged dictionaries (XamlControlsResources, custom themes, etc.).

children.description: Immutable (init-only) parameterized command descriptor. The action receives an argument of type T, enabling a single command definition to operate on different targets: var delete = new Command<Item> { Label = "Delete", Execute = item => Remove(item) }; MenuItem(delete, selectedItem)
children.label: Command<T>

children.description: Immutable (init-only) command descriptor that bundles an action with its metadata (label, icon, keyboard accelerator, enabled state). Define once, use in any surface: var save = new Command { Label = "Save", Execute = () => Save(), Icon = SymbolIcon("Save") }; AppBarButton(save) // toolbar MenuItem(save) // menu Button(save) // inline
children.label: Command

children.description: Bridges ICommand (MVVM/CommunityToolkit) to Command, enabling migration from ViewModel-based patterns to Reactor's declarative commanding. var reactorCmd = CommandInterop.FromCommand(viewModel.SaveCommand, "Save", icon: new SymbolIconData("Save"), accelerator: Accelerator(VirtualKey.S, Control));
children.label: CommandInterop

children.description: Rich contextual information harvested from the element tree during the scan. An AI agent uses this to generate semantically correct accessible names without needing to re-read the source code.
children.label: A11yContext

children.description: A single accessibility diagnostic finding from the scanner. Each finding maps to a specific WCAG 2.1 criterion and includes rich contextual information so an AI agent can generate intelligent fixes from the JSON export alone.
children.label: A11yDiagnostic

children.description: Tells an AI agent exactly which modifier to add and what value to use.
children.label: A11yFixSuggestion

children.description: Post-reconciliation accessibility scanner that walks the Reactor virtual element tree and produces structured diagnostics. Intended for DEBUG builds only — call via ReactorHostControl.EnableAccessibilityDiagnostics.

children.description: Describes the semantic role, value, and range of a composite component for assistive technology. Used with the .Semantics() modifier.

children.description: Custom AutomationPeer for SemanticPanel. Implements IRangeValueProvider and IValueProvider so screen readers can read the composite component's semantic role, value, and range. Analogous to SwiftUI's .accessibilityRepresentation {} and Compose's Modifier.semantics { role = Role.Slider }.

children.description: Process-wide feature flags that gate risky or in-progress behavior. Each flag is a plain mutable boolean so apps can flip it on startup; the defaults are chosen to preserve existing behavior.
children.label: ReactorFeatureFlags

children.description: The reconciler diffs old and new element trees and patches the real WinUI control tree.
children.label: Reconciler

children.description: Every visible thing on screen is a control. In Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) a control is the return value of a factory like TextBlock(...) or Button(...) — a plain element you compose, chain modifiers onto, and return from Render().
children.label: Controls catalog

children.description: Every form control in Reactor follows the controlled-input pattern: you own the value, you provide the change handler, and the control reflects your state. There is no two-way binding. The data always flows one direction.
children.label: Forms and input

children.description: When you need to render a list of data, Reactor provides three typed collection elements and a simple ForEach helper.
children.label: Collections

children.description: This page covers display text, inline rich text, rich-text editing, and media controls in Reactor.
children.label: Text and media

children.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s status and info controls report what the app is doing without stealing focus. Reach for them when the user needs to know something — a save succeeded, a long operation is running, a feature exists — and doesn't need to decide anything.
children.label: Status and info

children.description: ContentDialog, MenuFlyout, CommandBarFlyout and Popup: when to reach for each one, and how to drive them from component state.
children.label: Dialogs and flyouts

children.description: Reactor's data system provides a virtualized DataGrid<T> backed by a pluggable data source abstraction. You define columns (or auto-generate them), connect a data source, and the grid handles sorting, filtering, searching, selection, and inline editing.
children.label: Data system

children.description: ReactorD3 brings data visualization to Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor). The chart DSL provides high-level LineChart, BarChart, AreaChart, and PieChart factories that produce standard Reactor elements. You bind data, configure appearance with a fluent API, and the chart renders as native WinUI shapes on a Canvas.
children.label: Charting

children.description: Reactor.Advanced exposes the three Win2D canvas controls as Reactor elements. Add the package when you need immediate-mode drawing.
children.label: Win2D canvas

children.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) is a declarative UI framework for building native Windows desktop apps in pure C#. No XAML. No data binding. No view models. You describe your UI as a function of state, and Reactor keeps the screen in sync.
children.label: Overview

children.description: Install Reactor, scaffold a project, and grow it from hello world to a todo list and a calculator.
children.label: Quickstart

children.description: Coming soon — this page is the mental-model essay that frames Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) for new readers: UI as a function of state, why there is no XAML, when to reach for hooks, and how components compose.
children.label: Thinking in Reactor

children.description: If you already know XAML, Reactor is not a different Windows UI stack. It still renders real WinUI controls. The shift is in how you describe the UI: instead of splitting a page across XAML, bindings, converters, and code-behind, you return the UI directly from C# and let Reactor keep the native control tree in sync.
children.label: Coming from XAML

children.description: This page is for the XAML developer who wants the why behind Reactor's design.
children.label: Reactor vs XAML

children.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) at a glance. Every row links to the page that covers it in depth.
children.label: Cheat sheet

children.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s render loop has a small set of invariants. Most are enforced by analyzers, so a violation surfaces at build time with a specific code; the rest are conventions that the framework expects. This page lists them, names the analyzer where one exists, and shows the before/after pair so the catch is visible.
children.label: Rules of Reactor

children.description: Components are the building blocks of a Reactor app. Each component is a class with a Render() method that returns an element tree describing its UI.
children.label: Components

children.description: Hooks are functions you call inside Render() to manage state, side effects, and memoization. They replace the need for view models, event handlers, and lifecycle methods.
children.label: Hooks

children.description: UseEffect runs side effects — code that reaches outside the component's render function. Timers, data fetching, subscriptions, and DOM manipulation all belong in effects, not in Render().
children.label: Effects and lifecycle

children.description: Context lets you pass data through the component tree without threading it through every level of props. Define a Context<T>, provide a value at any level, and any descendant can read it with UseContext.
children.label: Context

children.description: A Command bundles an action with its metadata. Define it once and use it across buttons, menus, toolbars, and dialogs — the metadata stays consistent everywhere.
children.label: Commanding

children.description: Escape hatches for the few jobs the declarative model doesn't fit: error boundaries, memoized subtrees, element refs, direct property writes, view-model bridges, and custom hooks.
children.label: Advanced patterns

children.description: Reactor provides a small set of layout primitives that compose to build any screen structure. Every layout element accepts children and optional spacing.
children.label: Layout

children.description: FlexPanel is a Yoga-backed CSS Flexbox implementation, exposed through the FlexRow and FlexColumn factories. Reach for it when the layout needs alignment control, wrapping, or proportional sizing that VStack and HStack cannot express.
children.label: Flex layout

children.description: Color and style your UI with theme tokens, named-style modifiers, and resource overrides that follow the Light, Dark, and high-contrast themes automatically.
children.label: Styling and theming

children.description: Reactor exposes 36 named theme tokens on the static Theme class plus a Theme.Ref(string) escape hatch for any XAML resource key.
children.label: Theming tokens

children.description: Reactor animations are declarative. You set the target value (opacity, scale, translation) and attach a transition modifier.
children.label: Animation

children.description: Reactor's input surface is declarative: attach handlers via .On* modifiers and the reconciler wires WinUI events, auto-enables the matching flags (for example IsDoubleTapEnabled), and survives re-renders without re-subscribing the underlying WinUI event.
children.label: Input and gestures

children.description: Reactor uses a stack-based navigation model with type-safe routes. You define your routes as an enum, create a navigation handle with UseNavigation, and render the current page with NavigationHost.
children.label: Navigation

children.description: Most Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) apps start with the single window created by ReactorApp.Run. Larger desktop apps can open multiple native WinUI top-level windows with WindowSpec and ReactorApp.OpenWindow, while keeping the same declarative component model used inside a page.
children.label: Windows

children.description: Some shell-window ideas are possible on Windows only by leaving the safe Reactor contract. We document the recipe so expert apps can make an informed choice, but Reactor does not ship these primitives as first-class WindowSpec fields.
children.label: Advanced windowing

children.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor's docking system lets a single shell host multiple user-rearrangeable surfaces — the Visual Studio / VS Code / Photoshop / Figma layout idiom. Users drag tabs between groups, split panes, pin tool windows to a side, and tear panes out into floating sub-windows; layouts persist across sessions.
children.label: Docking windows

children.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s async hooks — UseResource, UseInfiniteResource, and UseMutation — replace the "one UseState for data, one for loading, one for error, one UseEffect to tie them together" pattern. They own the fetch lifecycle: cancellation on deps-change, drop late results after unmount, shared caching across siblings, and stale-while-revalidate by default.
children.label: Async resources

children.description: UsePersisted holds a value past a component re-mount — the user navigates away, the component unmounts, the user navigates back, and the captured state is still there.
children.label: Persistence

children.description: Reactor provides accessibility modifiers on every component. They map directly to WinUI's automation properties, so screen readers, keyboard navigation, and test tools work out of the box.
children.label: Accessibility

children.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s localization system wraps your component tree in a LocaleProvider that supplies an IntlAccessor to every descendant via context. You look up messages, format numbers and dates, and detect RTL layouts — all locale-aware, all reactive.
children.label: Localization

children.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s render loop is deterministic and synchronous. A Component mounted in a unit test renders, runs effects, accepts state updates, re-renders, and disposes through the same code path the WinUI host uses — minus the WinUI tree at the bottom.
children.label: Testing

children.description: A top-down performance workflow: take a trace with dotnet-trace or PerfView, learn what each span means, find the outlier, and reproduce a benchmark so a regression has a number behind it.
children.label: Performance

children.description: A Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) app is a normal WinUI 3 / Windows App SDK executable — dotnet publish produces the deployable artifact and the framework itself adds nothing exotic to the project file.
children.label: Packaging

children.description: Reactor's inner loop centers on dotnet watch and preview mode: you edit code, save, and see changes in a running window — no manual restart, no state-resetting class reload most of the time.
children.label: Dev tooling

children.description: The Visual Studio Embedded Preview hosts a live Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) component inside a Visual Studio tool window — Visual Studio 2026 (18.x), with the Visual Studio extension development workload. Unlike the VS Code preview, which streams screenshots, the Visual Studio extension embeds the real WinUI surface so mouse, keyboard, focus, popups, and accessibility tree inspection work against the running app.
children.label: VS extension

children.description: This page is about reading Reactor's diagnostics from a real app — not about adding new events.
children.label: Diagnostics

children.description: Reactor components can run inside WinForms applications using XAML Islands. The Reactor.Interop.WinForms package provides XamlIslandControl — a standard WinForms control that hosts a Reactor component tree with full keyboard, accessibility, and theming support.
children.label: WinForms interop

children.description: Host Reactor components inside a WPF app with a XAML island, until a first-class WPF host control ships.
children.label: WPF interop

children.description: Spec 050 changes controlled element-record properties from plain T to Optional<T>. Factory calls such as TextBox(text, setText), Slider(value, 0, 100, setValue), and ComboBox(items, index, setIndex) keep their existing plain-value signatures; they wrap the value in Optional<T>.Of(value) internally. Most app code therefore keeps compiling unchanged.
children.label: Optional<T> controlled props

children.description: Spec 054 intentionally removes a few legacy windowing fields in favor of more explicit shapes. The new APIs are additive except for the breaking changes below.
children.label: Windowing evolution

children.description: This page maps Reactor's runtime end-to-end so the rest of the Under-the-hood track has a shared diagram to point at.
children.label: Architecture overview

children.description: This page is the why behind the hooks surface. If you've come from XAML and INotifyPropertyChanged, the change of model is larger than the syntax.
children.label: Reactivity model

children.description: One description of the storage shape behind every hook — enough to debug a HookOrderException, predict whether UseState returns a stable setter, and know when reaching for UseRef is correct.
children.label: Hooks internals

children.description: This page absorbs the legacy docs/reference/reconciliation.md. The goal is one place to learn how Reactor diffs trees — the same information, in the structure the rest of the guide uses, plus the source pointers that let you verify it.
children.label: Reconciliation

children.description: This page is about when UseEffect fires and why.
children.label: Effects scheduling

children.description: Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) has one UI thread invariant: the reconciler, every hook setter, and every WinUI property write must happen on the thread that captured the dispatcher at app bootstrap.
children.label: Threading and dispatch

children.description: The Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) element pool recycles unmounted WinUI controls so a scroll-heavy list or fast-mounting subtree doesn't allocate a fresh TextBlock / Button / Border on every render.
children.label: Element pool

children.description: This page documents the data path between the reconciler and the WinUI control it edits. It is for anyone extending Reactor with a new native control, or debugging why an existing element does not update the way it should.
children.label: Control reconciler protocol

children.description: How to wrap a native Windows control as a Reactor element — a third-party WinUI control, a custom Control subclass, or an existing WinUI control that the built-in catalog has not yet covered.
children.label: Extending Reactor controls

children.description: This page is the runtime view of the same fluent chain that Styling introduces from the surface.
children.label: Modifier system

children.description: This page maps the four authoring surfaces onto the underlying compositor and explains the trade-offs that pick one surface over another.
children.label: Animation pipeline

children.description: This page covers the input subsystem from the routed-event boundary through the Reactor hooks that observe it.
children.label: Focus and input internals

children.description: "Source mapping" in Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) is the chain that ties a runtime artifact — an ETW event, a --preview overlay highlight, a thrown exception — back to the C# source that produced it.
children.label: Source mapping

children.description: This page walks through the Reactor analyzer pipeline end-to-end: how a diagnostic descriptor wires into the C# compilation, what happens on each InvocationExpression, and how to add your own rule.
children.label: Analyzer architecture

children.description: This page covers the internals of Reactor's devtools — the MCP server that external agents talk to, the in-app dev menu, the runtime overlays, and the gate that keeps the whole subsystem out of retail.
children.label: DevTools internals

children.description: This page covers what Reactor publishes, where to read it, and how to get a clean trace.
children.label: Perf instrumentation

children.description: A recipe is a small composition of Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) primitives that solves a real UI problem — login, master-detail, settings, paginated list, modal confirmation, multi-step form, search-with-suggestions, command palette, drag-to-reorder. The recipes here are not exhaustive apps; each is a single screen showing the pattern, and each ships a tiny doc app you can clone and adapt.
children.label: Recipes

children.description: A command palette is a filter-as-you-type list with a keyboard accelerator to open and Enter to execute. In Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) it's three UseState hooks, a static catalog of Command records, and an OnPreviewKeyDown handler — no menubar, no modal manager, no view model.
children.label: Command palette

children.description: Drag-reorder is a UseState<List<T>> plus a function that splices one item from one index to another. Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor)'s keyed reconciler does the rest — moves preserve identity, so the same row element keeps its focus, its hover state, and its place in the visual tree. Pointer drag is one entry point; an Alt+Up / Alt+Down keyboard shortcut is the second, and it carries the accessibility story.
children.label: Drag reorder

children.description: A Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) login form is four pieces working together: validated input, submit-gated state, an async call, and an error-display surface. The recipe below wires them with two UseState hooks and one UseMutation — no view model, no event handler classes, and no hand-rolled submitting / error flags.
children.label: Login

children.description: Master-detail in Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) is the canonical multi-pane shape: a list of records on one side, the selected record's details on the other. The whole thing is one UseState for the selected id and two slots in an HStack.
children.label: Master detail

children.description: The modal is an element you return conditionally. There is no special "open dialog" API — when open is true the tree includes the modal panel layered over the page; when it's false the modal element is absent and the page renders alone.
children.label: Modal dialog

children.description: A wizard form is a step-index UseState plus a switch on which step renders. The field state lives in the same component as the step index, so moving forward and back never loses what the user typed — Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) doesn't unmount the surrounding component when the visible slot changes.
children.label: Multi-step form

children.description: A paginated list is four states sharing one source of truth: an initial load, a populated list, a "load the next page" affordance, and a terminal "no more results." UseInfiniteResource owns all four in Microsoft.UI.Reactor (Reactor) — the component below pattern-matches on LoadState and reads Items directly; there is no local UseState for loading or errors.
children.label: Paginated list

children.description: The pattern is two slots: an input that owns the query string, and a dropdown that shows zero or more suggestions filtered against a catalog. UseMemo keys the filter on the query, so a re-render that didn't touch the query is free — important for the keyboard-up- arrow-down-arrow loop where the suggestion index changes but the query doesn't.
children.label: Search with suggestions

children.description: A settings page is many small persisted prefs side-by-side. Each preference is its own UsePersisted call with its own key — there's no central settings object that needs migration when one preference moves. The row layout is a single helper.
children.label: Settings page
